It's for iphone only holy moly its done. three years of lurking around here, couldnt be more proud are you sharing it anywhere? i'm in awe myself here, was rooting for this for so long - so happy to see it up and running and working https://github.com/dmtsys/eth2-nodes-uptime-monitoring first need this part, then yes! So push notification part is more ready than this one 😉 SMS is the wrong idea, I think .... I'm personally using the approach of having a `push notification` app directly installed on my iphone through my developer program. Input here is very welcome, what would be the best way for the other side of this problem, I think we can iterate very quickly in releasing this. This approach of being completely independent with no middlemen, `push notications` between me and my phone OS provider might not be for everyone (you need a developer account and installing the app directly not through the app store)... So maybe then the correct way would be to release this simple `notifier` app through my developer account and share it with others? I think it can be free forever since apple does not charge for notifications.... Not sure how to do it for Android... If anyone has better ideas for this push part, just write .... I'd rather not have to maintain a notifier app since it also needs a server component... Was looking for useful, free and reliable third party solutions, didn't find any. I've been working with small computers (RPi and others) for two years with a lightweight process running on each one of them and they all are sending push notifications on interesting events... so yes, this is awesome and should be part of anyone's arsenal.. you want to be notified in realtime if your important services have issues. Here is the code for iPhone notification receiver https://github.com/dmtsys/ios-notify -- anyone with developer account can install it on the phone, it will show a device token... this is to be plugged into long running process on your server which also monitors eth2 clients and then stuff will work. So, please write if interested in moving this forward... we have a lot of ingredients to make it happen but needs some more thinking / work. I'm not running any eth2 clients in production (for now) exactly to have more time for such things 😉 This is kind of my passion recently... // realtime notifications and process monitoring etc. my apologies for the late response, but i'll take a look at it thoroughly <@!97663671152410624> i really like the idea of push notifications and being independent on third party myself* are you on ios or android ? ios when you said iphone that's why i asked you if you can link 🙂 hah! too bad (joke). I was hoping for someone on android so we can move that part forward too but then yes, you can already use this notifier on your iphone but you need a cheap $100 / year Apple Developer account... I really recommend this... it's probably cheaper and more reliable than any 3rd party service you might use as a *middleman* do i need a dev license to install it? ok lol 🙂 that answers my question for Push you need yes i think i might even have one Apple Push notifications are included in developer accounts... you can install the app without it but it will only show you a token 😄 <@!97774605351010304> hey let's talk in private tomorrow... I can guide you through the process and we can document it... you have the exact case where I can immediately help with what I have then we present it to next set of people that need the same thing... and for sure someone will come that needs something else and then someone will add this to the setup / docs sounds good, let's chat tomorrow later in the day! 👋 thank you!! looks like new validators are now starting to join! 🚀 Do owners all get realtime push notifications on their ☎️ with minimal number of middlepeople possible ? 🤓 // update changed middlemen to middlepeople —— Btw there is also a push notification solution for open source tablets and regular PCs (darwin, linux, windows) without even Apple or Google as middlepeople. On the phone, of course, you need them but it’s ok, they’re around 99.99% reliable in delivering push notifications, my experience is that sometimes you do miss a single notification but it is almost never. Other solution is 100% reliable but you don’t see notifications unless you’re on a computer or if you have a cheap $150 open source tablet in front of you as one of home’s smartscreens. ... or if you hook your lightbulb in room to start blinking if there are issues with your validator client 🙂 also trivial to achieve... check out sonoff basic R3 modules 🤖 I recommend asking the ethstaker discord about hardware, monitoring, and notifications <@!97663671152410624> https://discord.gg/e84CFep Ok great, tnx. Will do tomorrow, enough computing for today 🙂 I think it's beneficial for validators to know if a slasher is present or not. Is the number of slashers being tracked? i mean on a website <@!375471494081282048> slashers don't advertise themselves, but you can safely assume that there is at least one person out there running a slasher lighthouse slashers are selfish by default though (in a good sense I feel), so they'll only include slashings in their own proposed blocks I forget if current slashers can catch _every_ slashable offense, but certainly the most likely ones can you please explain this part? I am running a slasher but on Prysm. Are they different on the amount they make? I am not sure about the default behavior of Prysm's slasher. I think they used to be selfish by default. Poking <@!311971895828283393> Our slasher broadcasts by default to the network We are rewriting our slasher close to end of the year, and we can reconsider this behavior Thanks. So what's the difference if it broadcasts to the network or is selfish? I guess what does it mean being selfish? I thought they have to broadcast and that's how a validator gets slashed... <@!311971895828283393> Selfish seems detrimental to the network. If there really is an attack going on it helps the network to know about it ASAP and shut down the relevant validators rather than dribbling out slashings over a period of days or weeks. selfish might be marginally profit maximizing for an individual, but I expect there to be at least a few non-selfish broadcast slashers that would likely make a selfish strategy moot (I run one of these.) thanks. well, then the specs should reward the whistleblowers 😉 it's not really possible without a commit/reveal scheme which greatly increases complexity and overhead.. Yep Jim nailed it. Imagine that you caught a bunch of slashings but youre not proposing a block until perhaps two weeks from now you are withholding that valuable data from the network the whistleblower reward, for just finding one slashing, is not really that big. Slashings should also (hopefully) be rare thanks +1 here, I do believe the hoarding strategy was good in medalla only because no one was running slashers besides <@602753420033785856> And he said that perhaps that may change on Lighthouse as well yeah, it's on my `TODO` list

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Selfish seems detrimental to the network.  If there really is an attack going on it helps the network to know about it ASAP and shut down the relevant validators rather than dribbling out slashings over a period of days or weeks.

excerpts.author: djrtwo
